title: Homeopathy | NHS inform
text:
Homeopathy
Homeopathy is a ‘treatment’ based on the use of highly diluted substances. Practitioners claim it can cause the body to heal itself.
There’s no good-quality evidence that homeopathy works.
A
2010 House of Commons Science and Technology Committee report
said that:
homeopathic remedies are no better than placebos (dummy medicines)
the principles of homeopathy are ‘scientifically implausible’
What is homeopathy?
Homeopathy is a complementary or alternative medicine (CAM). It’s different from conventional medicine and treatments.
Homeopathy is based on ideas developed in the 1790s by a German doctor called Samuel Hahnemann.
A central principle of the ‘treatment’ is that ‘like cures like’ – that a substance that causes certain symptoms can also help to remove those symptoms. A second central principle is based around a process of dilution and shaking, called succussion.
Practitioners (homeopaths) believe that the more a substance is diluted in this way, the greater its power to treat symptoms. Many homeopathic remedies are made of substances that have been diluted many times in water until there is none or almost none of the original substance left.
Does homeopathy work?
There’s no good-quality evidence that homeopathy is effective as a treatment for any health condition.
Is homeopathy available on the NHS?
Homeopathy is usually practiced privately. Homeopathic remedies are available from pharmacies.
What should I expect if I try homeopathy?
When you first see a homeopath they’ll usually ask you about:
any specific health conditions
your general wellbeing
your emotional state
your lifestyle
your diet
Based on this, the homeopath will decide on the course of treatment. Usually, homeopathic remedies are given as a pill, capsule or concentrated liquid.
Your homeopath may recommend that you attend follow-up appointments to check the effects on your health.
When homeopathy is used
Homeopathy is used to ‘treat’ a wide range of conditions.
Many practitioners believe that homeopathy can help with any condition.
Some of the most common conditions that people seek homeopathic treatment for are:
asthma
ear infections
hay fever
mental health conditions, such as depression, stress and anxiety
allergies, such as food allergies
dermatitis (an allergic skin condition)
arthritis
high blood pressure
There is no good-quality evidence that homeopathy is an effective treatment for these or any other health conditions.
Some practitioners also claim that homeopathy can prevent malaria or other diseases. There is no evidence to support this.
The
National Institute of Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
advises the NHS on proper use of treatments. NICE currently does not recommend that homeopathy should be used in the treatment of any health condition.
Are homeopathic remedies regulated?
There is no legal regulation of homeopathic practitioners in the UK. This means that anyone can practise as a homeopath, even if they have no qualifications or experience.
Voluntary regulation aims to protect patient safety. But it does not mean that there is scientific evidence that a treatment is effective.
Are homeopathic remedies safe?
Homeopathic remedies are generally safe. The risk of a serious adverse side effect from taking these remedies is thought to be small.
Some homeopathic remedies may contain substances that are not safe, or that interfere with other medicines.
Talk to your GP practice first if you’re considering:
stopping any medicine prescribed by a doctor
delaying any medical procedure or vaccination in favour of homeopathy
Risks of buying homeopathic medicines online or by mail order
Medicines bought online or by mail order are more likely to be fake, poor quality, or contaminated.
When buying online, it’s important to make sure you’re buying from a genuine supplier as some websites may appear to be trustworthy, but are fronted by bogus doctors or pharmacists.
